metadata.title: Myles Price sees one target in Week 2
metadata.description: Myles Price failed to catch his only target in the Vikings' 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Price remains minimally involved in the Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, recording one target or less in each of the first two games. The wideout remains best left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Returns kicks
metadata.description: Price recorded five kickoff returns for 179 yards and one punt return for 13 yards in Sunday's 39-22 win over the Packers.
metadata.analysis: The wide receiver also played on three offensive snaps but did not record a target. The second-year pro has yet to record a catch in his NFL career, but he seems to have a role as a returner.

metadata.title: Myles Price Making Push For Bigger Receiving Role?
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Myles Price logged an impressive preseason debut by catching all four of his targets for 51 yards and a touchdown on Saturday against the New York Giants. An undrafted free agent from Indiana, Price made the Vikings' 53-man roster last season and finished third in the NFL in kick return yards. The second-year pro is now competing with Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones for a secondary receiving role in the Vikings' offense, and Price's team-best 28-yard reception and acrobatic touchdown catch on Saturday certainly helped his cause. Still firmly behind Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and Jauan Jennings, Price won't factor into most standard formats, but he's a name worth knowing in formats that score return yards and deeper dynasty leagues.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Cleared for camp
metadata.description: Price passed his conditioning test and is good to go for training camp, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: The top kickoff and punt returner for the Vikings suffered an ankle injury in late Week 17 of last season. After an offseason of healing, Price is all set to suit up for training camp to attempt to defend his spot as the team's top return specialist. Tai Felton is the 24-year-old's primary competition for the role.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Won't play Sunday
metadata.description: Price (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Packers, Dane Mizutani of the St. Paul Pioneer Press reports.
metadata.analysis: Price didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday and is now in line to miss his first game of the season Sunday. The undrafted rookie from Indiana had a solid year while operating as the Vikings' primary return man, tallying 1,479 kick-return yards (third-most in the NFL) and 298 punt-return yards across 16 games. In his absence, expect Ty Chandler to operate as the Vikings' top return specialist in Week 18.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Sits out practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Price (ankle) was a non-participant in practice Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Price hurt his ankle Christmas Day versus Detroit and hasn't recovered enough to practice. With that in mind, it's uncertain if he'll be able to play in the Vikings' season finale against Green Bay on Sunday. Price has had just a bit role on offense this season, but he's been working as Minnesota's primary kick- and punt-returner, so he'd have to be replaced in those capacities if he can't suit up Sunday.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Won't return Thursday
metadata.description: Price (ankle) has been ruled out to return to Thursday's game against the Vikings.
metadata.analysis: Price suffered an ankle injury during the opening kickoff of Thursday's divisional matchup and will not retake the field. His next opportunity to return to action will come Sunday, Jan. 4 versus the Packers in Week 18.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Hurts ankle on opening kickoff
metadata.description: Price, who injured his ankle on the opening kickoff of Thursday's game against Detroit, is questionable to return, Andrew Kramer of the Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
metadata.analysis: With Price injured, Jalen Nailor is handling punt returns. Price collapsed while running back a kickoff and was untouched.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Racks up return yardage in win
metadata.description: Price returned six kickoffs for 143 yards in Sunday's 34-26 win over the Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: Price also took the field for a play on offense, but the depth receiver has yet to touch the ball as anything but a return man through his first 14 NFL games. While ball security (four fumbles) has been somewhat of an issue for Price, he's provided a boost to the Minnesota special teams with an average of 26.0 yards per kickoff return and 9.9 yards per punt return.

metadata.title: Myles Price - Makes impact with kick returns
metadata.description: Price returned five kickoffs for an average of 32.8 yards, including a 61-yard return, in Sunday's win at Detroit. He also had a 99-yard touchdown return called back due to a holding penalty. He had one punt return for seven yards.
metadata.analysis: Price's returns had a big impact on the victory, as it set up the Vikings with good field position early in the game. His 61-yard return was the team's longest since 2022, according to the Minnesota Star Tribune.
